title: Billy Evans Claims He Didn’t ‘Consent’ to ‘You Can See Everything’ Full Frontal Nude Scene and Thinks the ‘Color Grading Is Way Off’
description:
Billy Evans says he wasn’t fully on board with the plan to show, well, everything, in the hit documentary “You Can See Everything.”

	Elizabeth Hol
body:
Billy Evans says he wasn’t fully on board with the plan to show, well, everything, in the hit documentary “You Can See Everything.”

	Elizabeth Holmes’ partner is shown fully nude in the shower in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s buzzy film that shows the Theranos founder and her family in the days before she goes to prison, but he told CBS Sunday Mornings’ Matt Gutman “I didn’t want it.” 


	“Did you know you were doing the full Monty?” Gutman asks.
	

	“ I did not give consent to do that,” Evans claims. “Now, did I know they were filming me in the shower? Yes.  But we would film 16 hours a day, all sorts of things were filmed with assurances made. I was just as surprised as the rest of the country to have my whole body on camera for the world to see.”

Billy Evans asked Nathan Fielder and A24 to pixelate or remove a scene in “You Can See Everything” in which he appears fully nude in the shower.“It’s been an awkward experience in having, like, your kids’ teachers see that,” Evans told @CBSMATTGUTMAN. “It’s really… pic.twitter.com/1f6AnIIvDv— CBS Sunday Morning 🌞 (@CBSSunday) November 13, 2026


	However, Evans’ recent remarks on the scene contradict how the filmmakers describe the process. 

	“We were in the car ride on the way back from the gym and I said to Billy, ‘We will give you some time to shower,'” co-director Oppenheim told GQ. “And Billy responded, ‘Want to film me showering?’ I offered to film him in a way that could avoid seeing his genitals, but Billy said he didn’t care about being seen naked.”

	“It’s been an awkward experience and having your kids’ teachers see that.  It’s really uncomfortable. I’m not proud of it. I didn’t want it,” Evans tells Gutman in the interview which airs Sunday. 

	Evans claims he asked the filmmakers to at least pixelate the shower scene. “It’s been weird seeing the commentary about, ‘he’s just showing the world.’ I’m a confident guy. I am not that confident.”
	

	When Gutman asks if he contacted Fielder when he found out the scene would be included, Evans replies, “I communicated with them before the film came out. Both through lawyers and through myself. I was like, ‘Can you pixelate this?’ Is there anything you can do?  Because I had heard rumors from people who’d seen the film in the early screenings. And, they refused to do so.” 

	Though Gutman tells Evans he has a “very nice figure,” Evans doubles down in the interview that “I’m, asking them and pleading to them not to show this. Apparently, it was something that Nathan and A24 really wanted to show the world, but it’s not something I did. And it’s embarrassing. I’d also say the color grading is like, way off.”

	A24 had no comment.

title: Music Industry Moves: Diplo and Andrew Bergman Launch Bison Music; Debbie Gibson Inks With Downtown
description: Grammy-winning artist and producer Diplo and former Downtown Music CEO Andrew Bergman have joined forces to launch Bison Music, an independent musi
body:
Grammy-winning artist and producer Diplo and former Downtown Music CEO Andrew Bergman have joined forces to launch Bison Music, an independent music publisher. Bergman will serve as CEO, alongside COO Tom Lee, CCO Juba Lee and General Manager Jenny Ilibassi. (Pictured above, L-R: Tom Lee, Bergman, Diplo, Ilibasi, Juba Lee.)  

	Diplo initially formed the company “to bring together genre-defying songwriters and producers behind some of music’s most distinctive new voices,” according to the announcement, including the previously signed Picard Bros., Leclair, Maesic, Nitti, Kaien Cruz, BomboCat, Akira Evans, and Groupthink. Diplo and Bergman have joined forces to “transform Bison into a company dedicated to making fresh, original music written by real people to connect with a global audience,” it continues.
	

	“At a moment when it feels like music needs an injection of originality, our writers are in a position to shape where music goes next,” said Diplo. “Andrew and I are creating a home for those writers, with a team that knows how to develop them and a company built to back them for the long term.”

	Bergman added, “For me, there’s still nothing more exciting in music than discovering a great song from someone you’ve never heard of. That’s always been at the core of what makes music publishing a great business. And it’s what excited me about partnering with Diplo, one of the leading creative forces in the modern music business, and tmwrk, his management team and longtime business partners.”

	Bison is based in New York and Los Angeles. Further signings will be announced in the coming months.
	

	+ Debbie Gibson has signed with Downtown Music Publishing in a deal including administration for her current catalog and TV/Film Sync representation.

	“I’m so thrilled to be a part of the Downtown Music Publishing family in this creative era!” said Debbie Gibson. “I’m a songwriter at heart, first and foremost, so to be able to stretch my creativity and to have new sync opportunities before me is exciting. Not only is it such an honor to be amongst their prestigious roster of songwriters but I’m ecstatic to have the Downtown team look after my formerly unrepresented material and champion my new songs!”

	Bea Koramblyum, Global Head of Business Affairs & VP of Business Development, Downtown Music Publishing, comments: “Debbie Gibson is an extraordinary singer/songwriter whose music has stood the test of time. With a prolific legacy of work across four decades and an impressive musical theater background, she brings a wealth of creativity and talent to everything she does, and we’re excited to welcome her to Downtown Music Publishing, supporting the next chapter of her career.”

	+ Bossy Songs, the publishing company founded by Records co-founder and industry vet Barry Weiss with Sony Music Publishing has announced the extension of their relationship. Bossy Songs will continue to be supported and administered by SMP, with an office in New York and staff in Los Angeles and Nashville.

	Recent highlights from the company’s roster include Austin Corona’s work with Slayyyter and Charlie Ziman’s collaborations with Malcolm Todd,

	“I’m thrilled to be continuing our work with Sony Music Publishing, who have been incredibly supportive of our development” said Weiss. “Bossy Songs is proud to support fresh new emerging songwriters such as Austin Corona and Charlie Ziman (who are truly making themselves felt at the moment) and will be searching far and wide for new writers to add to our highly selective boutique roster.”

	Sony Music Publishing President, Head of US A&R Katie Welle said, “Barry and team have a proven track record of identifying and championing exceptional talent at Bossy Songs, they’ve built incredible foundation for future success. We are delighted to continue our partnership.”

	Wednesday, November 11
	

	Top communications firm Shore Fire Media has announced the promotion of Jaclyn D. Childress to president. A 13-year veteran of the firm and member of its leadership team since 2019, Childress (pictured above, left) will continue to head Shore Fire’s Nashville team, reporting to recently appointed CEO Angela Barkan, with a focus on sports, country music, reality TV and creators.

	Hired as a publicity coordinator in 2013, Childress rose through the company’s publicist ranks to become a vice president in 2021, then growing to senior vice president three years later.

	“In our short time working together, Jaclyn’s entrepreneurial nature has become very apparent,” said Barkan. “Besides overseeing our Nashville office, which works with prominent music businesses and talent, she signed our first creator in 2019 and has established our thriving sports practice. I know she will continue to help build the business as an integral part of our executive leadership team.”

	+ Epic Records has promoted Ayanna Wilks to Senior Vice President, Head of Publicity, and Tina Ibañez to Senior Vice President, Creative & Content, effective immediately, the company annoucned. Both will report to Ezekiel Lewis, Chairman and CEO of Epic Records.

	Wilks (pictured above, center) will lead Epic’s publicity department from Los Angeles. She joined Epic in 2019 as Senior Director of Publicity and rose to Vice President before stepping into her new role. Previously, she held roles with Wilhelmina Models, Roc Nation and Diane von Furstenberg.

	In her new role, Ibañez (pictured above, right) will lead Epic’s creative department from New York. She joined Epic in 2021, where she has shaped the visual worlds of artists across the roster.

	Ibañez was previously a Senior Art Director at Sony Music, where she earned a Grammy Award with fellow creative Brett Kilroe. She began her career at design studio Trooper.

	“Great artists need partners who can tell their story and build their world. Ayanna and Tina do both at the highest level. Ayanna understands how to shape an artist’s narrative and connect it to culture, and Tina has a rare gift for turning an artist’s vision into something you can see and feel. Together, they’ve helped define what Epic stands for. As we invest in the next generation of Epic talent, they’re exactly the leaders I want building it with us,” Lewis said.
	

	+ The Ally Coalition has announced its 12th Annual Talent Show will take place Tuesday, December 15 at the Jack H. Skirball Center for the Performing Arts in New York City, at 7:30pm. Tickets will be open for pre-sale this Wednesday, November 11 and to the general public Thursday, November 12 at 10am ET.

	Created and curated by TAC Founder, Jack Antonoff, the annual Talent Show has raised more than $2 million to support unhoused LGBTQ+ youths and has featured performances by Taylor Swift, Lana Del Rey, Sabrina Carpenter, Rachel Zegler, Phoebe Bridgers, Hayley Williams, Hasan Minhaj, Kasey Musgraves, Florence Welch, Jason Isbell, Clairo, and St. Vincent, among dozens of others.

	“The Talent Show exists in its own special world that we have built over the last eleven years: bringing together my favorite artists to play a small room in New York for our people,” notes Jack Antonoff. “All proceeds go to The Ally Coalition and our work supporting the homeless LGBTQ+ community – means the world to me and everyone who works hard to make this night happen every year.”

	+ The Recording Academy has promoted Joanna Chu to SVP of Awards, Susan Stewart to VP of the Songwriters & Composers Wing, and Michael Nieporent has been named SVP of Global Partnerships & Business Development.

	Chu previously served as VP of Awards for five years, leading the department through all aspects of Grammy season and reinforcing key Academy initiatives throughout the Awards process. Stewart has led the S&C Wing since she helped establish it in 2020 — first announced on the 63rd Grammy Awards Telecast — and has grown it to represent nearly half of the Academy’s voting membership. Nieporent joins the Academy with more than 17 years of experience building and leading partnerships across entertainment, media and live events, including the Academy of Country Music Awards, the American Music Awards, and the Billboard Music Awards.

	+ Sony Music Publishing U.K. has signed songwriter-artist Natalie Findlay, which includes all future works. Her recent work includes co-written songs with Suki Waterhouse (“Good Looking”), Ashe (“Swan Lake”), joining a discography that includes releases from Remy Bond, Blossoms and Declan McKenna.

	Findlay said, “I’m really happy to be joining Sony Music Publishing for my next chapter. I’ve always been drawn to artists with something unique to say and to create music that feels real and exciting. I’m lucky to have a new team around me who understands that and shares my enthusiasm for what’s ahead.”
	

	+ Prescription Songs has signed Phil Leigh, a Los Angeles–based songwriter-producer whose credits include Le Sserafim’s “Spaghetti,” Twice’s “Hi Hello,” ANOTR’s “Paradise,” and Jason Derulo and Michael Bublé’s “Spicy Margarita.” He has also collaborated on songs by Beyoncé, David Guetta, the Chainsmokers and J Balvin, with forthcoming releases from Marshmello, ANOTR, and Purple Disco Machine.

	Leigh said, “Life is the best! And a HUGE part of why I feel that way is because of music. I’m truly obsessed with it and I don’t take for granted that I’ve been allowed to spend my life feeling, playing and creating professionally. I’ve been close with the Prescription Songs family for a very long time and it means the world to me that I’m now officially a part of it, working with them. They match my freak, and I’m so grateful that they are the people that I’m doing this with.”

	+ TuneCore has named Tash Shah as the company’s new Vice President, Global Marketing. She will report to Chief Business Officer Brian Miller. In her role, she will lead worldwide marketing strategy, spanning brand and creative, customer acquisition, lifecycle and retention, and product marketing.

	Shah joined TuneCore in 2023 as Vice President, International, where she led international strategy, held P&L responsibility for each market, and managed teams across 17 countries. Prior to joining TuneCore, she spent 12 years at Spotify, where she served as the company’s first Head of Marketing in the UK, enacting some of the platform’s earliest in-house Artist Marketing campaigns and securing partnerships with the BBC, Nike, and more.

	Miller commented, “Independent artists who are already building an audience need more than a place to upload music. They need a partner that helps them grow. Tash has spent three years understanding what those artists need, and she has the vision to make TuneCore the platform they choose to build their careers on. I’m excited to see her lead our global marketing team into this next chapter.”

	+ Anuel AA collaborator La Greña has signed with Vydia in conjunction with ShowOff Gang Music for the upcoming release of his album “Diferente,” due on Nov. 27. La Greña will drop the forthcoming project’s first single “Todos Loco,” on Friday.
	

	Speaking on the signing, ShowOff Gang Music President Jason “JT” Thomas said, “La Greña represents the kind of raw talent, authenticity, and star power we’re building ShowOff Gang Music around. Partnering with Vydia to introduce him to the world is more than just a strategy; it’s a statement that we believe in his vision, his sound, and his ability to make a global impact. We’re not just signing an artist; we’re investing in the next major voice coming out of the Dominican Republic.”

title: How ‘Tuner’ Sound Designer Johnnie Burn Used Dolby Atmos to Mimic Hyperacusis
description: Johnnie Burn, the Oscar-winning sound designer behind “Hamnet” and “The Zone of Interest,” found Daniel Roher’s “Tuner” to be one of his most perso
body:
Johnnie Burn, the Oscar-winning sound designer behind “Hamnet” and “The Zone of Interest,” found Daniel Roher’s “Tuner” to be one of his most personal projects to date.

	In the film, Leo Woodall plays Niki, an expert piano tuner with acutely sensitive hearing that is sometimes debilitating — in fact, it’s one reason Niki hasn’t chased his dreams of being a pianist. But it’s perfect for his profession, and he finds out that it’s perfect for safecracking too. But Niki gets in too deep with a gang of thieves as he becomes involved in a lovely relationship with gifted musician and composer Ruthie (Havana Rose Liu). Oscar-winning documentarian Daniel Roher (“Nalavany”) takes viewers on a thrill ride centered on hyperacusis, a rare condition that affects one’s hearing.
	

	Burn tells Variety he experienced a mild version of hyperacusis in his late teens. “People who suffer from it chronically go through a devastating experience of not being able to possibly recover or go outside. I had this situation where I witnessed an explosion, and I went 100% deaf for about 20 minutes. When my hearing came back, I had hyperacusis and extreme sensitivity to everyday sounds.”

	When Burn received the script, his first response was, “I know what this is.” His next step was researching what this world sounded like. To understand that soundscape, Burn had microphones placed inside his eardrums and went about his daily life. “I was recording things from my ears’ point of view, and playing it back later to understand what things become fairly loud that your brain would normally dial out because they’re not threatening, such as putting a pan in the dishwasher or even a shower tap — everyday sounds that can break through.”
	

	The goal was to teach audiences how Niki interacts with his environment and what the dangers are. Burn worked to create various sound levels, including one from Niki’s point of view that allowed audiences to understand his world and another where Niki has ear defenders on, which help restrict sound. One example Burn gives is when Niki sits at a traffic light and a motorbike comes alongside him. “That’s really about teaching the audience that there are these different states in which he can be listening to things,” Burn adds. “The aim was to have the audience experience it alongside him, which is obviously with hyperacusis. It’s not like deafness or anything. It’s a situation where everyday sounds can become dangerously loud for you.”

	Burn drove that home in the Dolby mix of the film, pushing the sound design. He and Roher sat in the mix, fine-tuning every decibel. “The different points of view of Niki’s hearing were a fundamental part of whether or not the film worked. I believe we cracked that. The Dolby Atmos mix was a further development of that because it gave us the ability to predominantly play sound at a much greater volume all around us.”

schema.headline: How ‘Tuner’ Sound Designer Johnnie Burn Used Dolby Atmos to Mimic Hyperacusis

title: Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival: Genre Mashups, a Vibrant Brazil and an Award for the One-Off Paulina García
description: Honoring Paulina García (“Gloria”), highlighting the latest from great and fast emerging Latin American directors, the 52nd Huelva Ibero-American F
body:
Honoring Paulina García (“Gloria”), highlighting the latest from great and fast emerging Latin American directors, the 52nd Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival lifts off Nov. 13 as a film event for our times.

	Bulwarked by fast-recovering Europe and Asia, global film production in 2025 edged up to 7,707  features, higher than pre-pandemic levels of 2017-19. Latin America was no exception, up 2%.


	In such a context, film festivals are worth their weight in gold as quality filters, and few are more curated than the Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival. TIFF screened 293 films in Official Selection this year. Huelva’s total lineup will feature around 100 films, festival director Manuel H. Martín tells Variety.
	

	That’s par for the course for Huelva which will keep its main section, including a main feature and short film competition, Talento Andaluz, framing event films from Andalusia, and Acento. Cine Español, a national movie panorama.

	“For us, it’s fundamental to have a festival format in line with Huelva, a friendly, close city where you can walk to places,” says Martín. “We’re aiming for a varied quality lineup with premieres for Spain and a chance to catch-up on Spanish films released during the year, but we’re not interested in growing year after year in volume.”

	Huelva’s main competition will, indeed, feature just 12 titles, two more out-of-competition.

	Amaia Salamanca, a star of “Grand Hotel” and “Velvet” and key in the lift-off of Spanish TV as an international phenomenon, will pick up a Luz Prize at Huelva’s opening Gala, as will Patrick Criado, good in Pedro Almodóvar’s “Bitter Christmas” and sensational in 2023 TV series “Nights in Tefia.”
	

	However tightly curated, Huelva’s lineup also allows a broader vision of which ways Latin American cinema and film industries are heading in Latin America. A few brief provisional takes as the 52nd Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival unpools in Andalusia, running through Nov. 21:

	Multi-Genre Mashups

	Where’s Latin America’s cinema at? Some of its most exciting movies, as in world cinema at large, is genre bending and blending. “The Riverbank” “traverses the classic erotic thriller to experiment with tropical noir, crime drama, magical realism and even a hint of whodunnit,” Variety observes, all inspired by and exploring the reality of Recife life, director Enock Carvalho notes. “The Bovine with the Curved Horns” braids myth, oral tradition, Colombia’s armed conflict and downbeat daily life. “Days Off,” Argentine Luciana Mariani’s surprising debut melds coming of-age and sci-fi beats, as Bego, 12, experiments with shifting – the move to an alternative reality – during a solar eclipse.

	Paulina García

	García’s receives this year’s City of Huelva Prize, the festival’s highest honor. It is a measure of García’s stature that in Variety’s appreciation of Sebastián Lelio, comparing Julianne Moore’s performance in “Gloria Bell,” inspired by “Gloria,” which won García a Berlin Silver Bear in 2015, Variety does not call Moore’s a better turn but just different. “Gloria” was Lelio’s and García breakout, turning her into one of Latin America’s few performers courted by U.S. auteurs, in part for her enormous range. She is “a funny and resilient force of nature” in “Gloria,” but equally she can act a gravely ailing mother in Huelva 2026 title “Julia’s Flowers,” fading, irascible, frail, seemingly light-bodied, child-like but still, at times, capable of cognizance.

	Brazil Flexes Its Muscles

	No country in Latin America has broken out to international recognition more than Brazil. Last year Walter Salles’ “I’m Still Here” won an Oscar. This year, Kleber Mendonça Filho’s “The Secret Agent” scored four Academy Award nominations. Brazil has no film of such scale this year. What it does have, however, is underscored at Huelva. It has funding from its government, “Funk” supported by a classic financing combination of public sector bank BRDE, fund FSA and the Ancine national agency. Brazil also has vibrant regional and municipal film scenes. “Funk” is set in Rio, supports by RioFilme. “The Riverbank” forms part of Recife’s vibrant film scene. The consequences? Films which have the singularity and relevance of auteur cinema but high production standards.
	

	Multi-Partner Co-Production

	Or it’s got there already. Sometimes the partners align in a single territory, such as “The Bovine with the Curved Horns,” produced by Colombia’s La Fortaleza Films, Congo Films, Universidad del Magdalena, Lightbox, Pablo Mondragón, De La Tierra Producciones and Soretti Films. Or co-producers stack up internationally, such as on Lucila Mariani’s “The Days Off,” produced by Argentina’s Maravillacine (“Marilyn,” “Under the Flags, the Sun”), alongside Brazil’s Persona Non Grata Pictures and Vulcana Films (“Hard Paint,” “Night Stage”), with Mexico’s Woo Films (“Pedro Páramo,” “Noise”) and Valiente Films as co-producers. Co-production these days is a sign of necessity and partners wanting to buy into exciting propositions.

	Women Reach Some Parity

	Huelva’s competition lineup features seven films by men, though two of those – “Julia’s Flowers” and “Funk” – have women protagonists. Four of the 12 have queer lead characters. Add Manuela Martelli’s “The Melting” and Fernanda Tovar’s “Sad Girls” and seven of the 14 official section movies are helmed by women. Overall, of Hueva’s around 100 titles, half are directed by women, notes Martin. Four of the 14 films have LGBTQ lead characters. Huelva is, however, something of an exception when it comes to festivals and women’s films and the world. LGBTQ freedoms remains a barometer of larger freedoms in many Latin American films, such as “Riverbank,” whose leads face the brutal antagonism of members of an Evangelical church.

	Latin America’s – and Huelva’s – Issue Cinema

	“We attempt to program films which have a variety of themes, such as might be LGBTQ, mourning or mental health, subjects which can engage and concern society,” says Martín. Huelva’s lineup, as so much of Latin American cinema, deals with issues. In Latin America, the issues are impossible to ignore, Nobel Prize Winning novelist Mario Vargas Llosa said decades ago. That remains true, however, down to this day.

schema.headline: Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival: Genre Mashups, a Vibrant Brazil and an Award for the One-Off Paulina García

title: 10 Huelva Festival Standouts From ‘La Bola Negra’ to a Vibrant ‘Funk’ Musical and the Latest from ‘Dive’ Director Lucía Puenzo
description: Look at the U.S. summer box office and beyond. ‘The Odyssey’ is a film made for the public, but from a personal vision, as indeed is ‘La Bola Negra
body:
Look at the U.S. summer box office and beyond. ‘The Odyssey’ is a film made for the public, but from a personal vision, as indeed is ‘La Bola Negra,’” says Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival Director Manuel H. Martín.

	This year’s 52nd edition indeed screens “La Bola Negra,” as well as “The Beloved,” in a catch-up Accent Cine Español panorama in a year when Spanish cinema has never had it so good, fielding three titles in Cannes main competition: Pedro Almodóvar’s “Bitter Christmas, “Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved” and “La Bola Negra.”
	

	Talento Andaluz frames two notable doc features from an active regional documentary film scene.

	Above all, its 12-title main competition, spotlights notable Latin America debuts and the latest from directors who have stood out for their auteurist personality, social concerns and crossover style, the kind of films Huelva loves to program.

	Variety profiles some of this year’s standouts:

	“After Elena” “Después de Elena,” ( Shawn Garry, Cine Matriz, Doc: Co, Creative Content, Italy’s Zoe Films, Fundacion Rio and By Lace Films, Chile, Colombia, Italy)

	A dark absurdist comedy, Toronto 2026 world premiere and Garry’s second feature following on “Desierto Sur,” here starring Alfredo Castro, a Pablo Larraín go-to actor and Nicolás Zárate, attracting heat after “Red Hanger.” Castro’s Roberto, 70, wants nothing more than to retreat into his family home after wife Elena’s death, but is forced to take in his three adult children and offspring. In their comically halting reconnection, Roberto finds a way to navigate grief. Castro plays against type, abandoning the “heightened performances I’m used to” for “strict, grounded realism,” he told Variety. Gabriela Sandoval produces out of her Cine Matriz label.
	

	“Anguita. El Hombre de los Tres Siglos,” (Hugo Cabezas,

	Spain)

	An admirably and intensely crafted doc-feature portrait of Julio Anguita, a first communist Mayor of Cordoba (1978-86), president of Izquierda Unida (1987-2000), a national left-wing anti-capitalist alliance and third political force in Spain in the 1990s. This is a intimate, tempered and nuanced portrait of an orator, a man of elegance, humanity and a virtue, which was also for his critics his major failing: His intransigences, his unwillingness to dessert principles in polices, whatever the political gain. Directed by Hugo Cabezas (“Atín Aya,” “Últimas unidades”), mixing testimony and archival footage, produced by Seville-based La Favorita, backed by pubcaster RTVA.

	“The Beloved,” (“El ser querido,” Rodrigo Sorogoyen, Spain, France)

	Though “La Bola Negra” was this year’s Cannes sensation, among other Cannes main competition films, “The Beloved” still rated for its fans as one of the strongest. “Bardem is powerful as a filmmaker directing his estranged daughter in Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s making-of-a-movie drama,” said Variety. It is also Sorogoyen’s most daring film to date, slicing and dicing the central story of a father-daughter re-encounter from multiple character POVs, so dazzling different formats, where father and daughter battle through to some sort of agreement to a common story about the past and present. Like “La Bola Negra” and “‘Sirāt,” part of Movistar Plus’ first movie slate, giving directors budgets to make the movie they need to tell. And it tell in the results.

	“La Bola Negra,” (Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, Spain-France)

	“I want to do an LGBTQ+ movie for everyone and to be the gayest, biggest war movie ever,” co-director Javier Ambrossi told Variety co-editor in chief Ramin Setoodeh at last week’s Miami FiLm Festival. Los Javis may have done just that, moreover. The Cannes Festival’s most prominent Oscar hopeful, the big question about “La Bola Negra” is how far it can go, in Academy Award nominations and wins and box office in Spain, where its €38.5 million ($42.75 million) and counting makes it the third highest-grossing Spanish movie in Spain in history. Netflix’s Dec. 2 bow will add further global resonance to the milestone title.
	

	“Funk,” (Ali Muritiba, Brazil)

	A “revolutionary film,” says Muritiba, centering “Black joy” in a musical where there are no gunshots. That’s not to say the film doesn’t show any suffering. Sassy, smart, talented, sexually uninhibited on stage in her MC Sabrina persona, Sabrina (Duda Santos) dreams of making it in the world of Brazilian funk. Her success comes at large personal sacrifice, however. A brainchild of major Brazilian producer-director Hector Dhalia (“Adrift,” “Criminal Code”), producer Manoel Rangel and Muritiba, pursuing a through line with other movies from the director set on an axis of loneliness and desire,Variety notes.

	“Gugu’s World,” (Allan Deberton, Brazil)

	“A radiant queer coming-of-age charmer from Brazil,” Variety saidin its review of Allan Deberton’s “generous character study” of a queer pre-teen, turning on Gugu, 12, and his relationship with his grandmother, increasingly afflicted by dementia. “Gugu’s World” walked off with a 2026 Berlin KPlus Generation jury prize. Drawing more heat, it now figures as Brazil’s Intl. Feature Film Oscar entry, announced after Huelva zeroed in on the film for competition says Martín. Produced by Brazil’s Biônica Filmes through Projeto Paradiso’s Incubator initiative and sold by M-Appeal which cherrypicks sales on some of the best films in Latin American cinema.

	“Julia’s Flowers,” (“Las Flores De Julia,” Cris Tapia Marchiori, Argentina, Chile)

	Shot in a completely different register to Tapia Marchiori’s one-shot “Gunman,” screened at IFF Rotterdam, “Julia’s Flower” weighs in as a quiet daughter-mother acceptance melodrama. In it, Julia returns to her home village as Álvaro, aged 17, to hand over power of attorney over her gravely ailing mother (Paulina Garcia). Set in the vast lakes and rugged rocky mountains of Mendoza, a midlife identity tale framed by the performances of transexual actress Mariana Genesio Peña and Paulina García. Humor-laced, mellow, its tone is set by a measured piano score and Marchori’s sense of breathing larger sense to a film by camerawork not dialog, as in the film’s moving final scenes.

	“200 Lives, Paco Rabal,” (“200 vidas, Paco Rabal,” Vanesa Benítez, Spain-France-Mexico)
	

	The doc-feature, a San Sebastián world premiere and centenary tribute to Francisco Rabal, casts us in a dreamlike state. We track the life of the prolific actor who worked with everyone; Buñuel, Antonioni and Saura, and Almodóvar. Vanesa Benítez skips talking heads, allowing Rabal to narrate himself through newly found footage and audio. A Franco-era star who journeyed to collaborate with those in sharp opposition to the dictator, his words reveal him, in Benítez’s words, as “a child who wanted to return to the paradise of childhood.” The doc doubles as a tour of 20th-century cinema, from Nouvelle Vague to Spain’s ’80s.

	“Pepita, the Gunslinger,” (“Pepita, La Pistolera” Lucía Puenzo, Argentina,)

	Most anything Argentina’s Lucía Puenzo does is worth tracking. Breaking out from the get-go as an A-List festival auteur, her debut, 2007’s “XXY,” won Cannes Critics Week Grand Prix. She has gone on to pioneer genre-driven premium TV in Latin America (“La Jauría”) and champion women’s freedoms, battle against abuse (“Mexico 80,” “Dive”) and empowerment, as in “Pepita the Gunslinger.” Starring Luisana Lopilato (“In Love and in Hate”), it is inspired by the real-life figure of Margarita Di Tullio who rebels against the deaths of fellow sex workers in 1980s Mr del Plata by founding her own brothel and nightlife business empire.

	“The Riverbank,” (Matheus Farias and Enock Carvalho, Brazil-Germany)

	A Locarno 2026 Special Jury Prize Winner and Best Fiction Feature Film at this year’s Rio Film Festival, Brazil’s biggest film event, “The Riverbank” also marks the latest from Recife’s vibrant film hub, brought to world notice by “The Secret Agent.” Young janitor Izaquiel (Caique Copque), meets statuesque fisherman Jeremias (Ítalo Martins) in the depths of Recife’s mangrove forest, as his job at an evangelical church exposes its links with politics and death squad violence. Picked up by MPM Premium and Premium Films, an auteur multi-genre tropical noir thriller dosed by magical realism and announcing major new voices in Brazilian cinema.

schema.headline: 10 Huelva Festival Standouts From ‘La Bola Negra’ to a Vibrant ‘Funk’ Musical and the Latest from ‘Dive’ Director Lucía Puenzo

title: ‘Dept. Q’ Crew Member Dies on Set in Edinburgh After Season 2 Wrapped Filming
description: A crew member working on the Netflix series “Dept. Q” has died on set in Edinburgh after filming wrapped for Season 2. The production company behin
body:
A crew member working on the Netflix series “Dept. Q” has died on set in Edinburgh after filming wrapped for Season 2. The production company behind the series, Left Bank Pictures, said it is “deeply shocked and saddened by the tragic death.”

	The man has not been named, and specific details about the incident have yet to be reported. Police were called to FirstStage Studios in Scotland on Thursday afternoon after the crew member was seriously injured. Emergency services responded to the incident, but the man ultimately died.
	

	The death took place after cameras stopped rolling, meaning the incident could have taken place during the dismantling of sets. Scottish police confirmed that the death is not being treated as suspicious, “however, inquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances.”

	“We are deeply shocked and saddened by the tragic death of a member of our ‘Dept. Q’ crew,” a spokesperson for Left Bank Pictures said in a statement. “Our thoughts are with their family, friends and colleagues at this incredibly difficult time, and we are offering support for those affected.”

	Representatives for Netflix did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment. 

	A popular and award-nominated crime series, “Dept. Q” is one of Netflix’s biggest international hits in the past few years. The show stars Matthew Goode as emotionally scarred detective Carl Morck, who returns to police work months after a traumatizing injury. The first season aired on Netflix in May 2025 and was renewed for a second season a few months later.

title: Margot Robbie to Star in A24’s ‘The Week of Pain’ From ‘The Drama’ Director Kristoffer Borgli
description: Margot Robbie will star in A24 and Square Peg’s “The Week of Pain” from “The Drama” writer-director Kristoffer Borgli, Variety has confirmed. A24 i
body:
Margot Robbie will star in A24 and Square Peg’s “The Week of Pain” from “The Drama” writer-director Kristoffer Borgli, Variety has confirmed. A24 is set to produce and finance the project. Ari Aster and Lars Knudsen’s Square Peg banner will also produce alongside Dilemma Films and Robbie’s LuckyChap. 

	Plot details for “The Week of Pain” remain under wraps, but considering Borgli’s previous works, which include “Dream Scenario” and “Sick of Myself,” it’s safe to assume it will be another squirmy drama with streaks of cringe-out humor. Square Peg and A24 recently collaborated with Borgli on April’s “The Drama,” which starred Robert Pattinson and Zendaya. The film, an intimate original dramedy about a wedding week derailed by a childhood secret, was a box office smash, grossing $135 million worldwide against a slim $28 million budget. 
	

	Robbie most recently appeared in the steamy literary romance “Wuthering Heights” for Warner Bros. Audiences couldn’t resist a big-screen affair between the “Barbie” superstar as Cathy and Jacob Elordi as her mysterious love interest, Heathcliff, and the film rocketed to $241 million worldwide. Coming up for Robbie is an “Ocean’s 11” prequel. She will star alongside Bradley Cooper, who is also directing, presumably as the mom and dad of George Clooney’s Danny Ocean. Robbie revealed at CinemaCon 2026 that the film will follow an “epic heist at the 1962 Monaco Grand Prix.” Clooney, in a completely separate sequel, is getting the band back together from the 2001 original for one last ride. 

	Robbie is represented by Entertainment 360, CAA, Narrative, Aran Michael Management and attorney Jeff Bernstein. Borgli is repped by UTA.

title: Netflix’s ‘Magic the Gathering’ Animated Series Drops First Look at ‘Planeswalker,’ Set for 2027
description:
Netflix has unveiled the first-look image from its upcoming animated series based on “Magic the Gathering.” 

	The series, titled “Planeswalker,” i
body:
Netflix has unveiled the first-look image from its upcoming animated series based on “Magic the Gathering.” 

	The series, titled “Planeswalker,” is set to debut in 2027, with an exact release date to be announced later. 

	The official description of the series states: 

	“‘Planeswalker,’ an epic fantasy saga from the world of ‘Magic: The Gathering,’ chronicles the fierce clash between formidable mages known as Planeswalkers. At the center of this struggle for power and survival burns Chandra, a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past. Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence. As the line between victory and annihilation grows thinner, a single spark determines the fate of thousands of worlds.”
	

	The show is produced in partnership with Hasbro Entertainment and Wizards of the Coast. Terry Matalas and Cindy Appel serve as executive producers and co-showrunners.  Patrick Osborne is an executive producer and supervising director. Gabriel Marano will also serve as executive producer and Lauren Chavez-Myers will co-executive produce for Hasbro Entertainment. Daisy West is a producer on the series. Digic provides the animation. 

	The show has been in the works at Netflix for over six years at this point. Originally announced in 2019, the first iteration of the series was overseen by the Russo brothers of MCU fame. But then Jeff Kline was announced as the new executive producer and creative lead on the show in 2021 after the Russos departed over creative differences, with Brandon Routh being announced as voicing the series lead not long after. 
	

	There was then no news about the series until 2024, when Routh gave an interview in which he said he believed the show was “not happening” anymore. Not long after that, Matalas was named the new showrunner. 

	The “Magic: The Gathering” tabletop card game was created by Richard Garfield and first released in 1993. Since then, the game has spawned a digital game, esports league, comic book series, and a best-selling novel. It has been published in 11 languages in over 70 countries.

title: ‘Hold Onto Me’ Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: ‘I Really Feel Like We’re Underdogs’
description: It’s been a whirlwind year for Cypriot filmmaker Myrsini Aristidou, whose 2026 started with a triumphant trip to Park City, where her debut feature
body:
It’s been a whirlwind year for Cypriot filmmaker Myrsini Aristidou, whose 2026 started with a triumphant trip to Park City, where her debut feature, “Hold Onto Me,” won the audience prize in the World Cinema Dramatic competition at Sundance. Then, in September, the film made history when it was tapped to represent Cyprus in the international feature race at the Academy Awards — the first time the small island nation has submitted a film for what was formerly the foreign-language category.
	

	Now, after a pair of sold-out screenings at the Thessaloniki Film Festival, where “Hold Onto Me” plays in the Meet the Neighbors+ competition, Aristidou is packing her bags for the U.S., where her scrappy debut begins its Oscar campaign.

	The 36-year-old has barely had time to catch her breath.

	“It’s a great achievement, but it brings a lot of responsibility and a lot of work that comes with that,” she says. “I have no idea of what our chances are, to be honest. I’ve never done this before. Cyprus is a very small country. I really feel like we’re underdogs. We don’t have a lot of money to do the campaign. We’re just doing the best we can.”

	“Hold Onto Me” follows free-spirited 11-year-old Iris, played by newcomer Maria Petrova, whose summer fun is interrupted by the arrival in town of her estranged father Aris, played by Christos Passalis (“Dogtooth”). A reluctant dad who’s only returned for his own father’s funeral, Aris rebuffs his daughter’s efforts to reconnect. But her persistence gradually thaws his heart, offering the hope — if not the promise — of eventually rebuilding their fractured relationship.
	

	In a glowing Sundance review, Variety’s Carlos Aguilar praised the “heartfelt drama,” noting that while the film “treads in familiar waters,” Aristidou’s “astute writing and assuredly bittersweet performance take the story into singular, surprising places.” “Hold Onto Me” is produced by Filmblades and One Six One Films, in co-production with Fredo Pictures and Graal Films. Cercamon is handling world sales.

	Speaking to Variety in Thessaloniki, Aristidou explains how the film marked a homecoming after seven years in the U.S., where she studied film as an undergraduate at New York City’s Pratt Institute before getting her master’s degree at NYU.

	“It was a big decision to leave the U.S. and…go back to my country and make a Greek-language film and shoot it where I grew up,” she says. “It was important to me to capture the textures of everyday life [in Cyprus]: the worn-out backdrops,the slow movement of time and the raw emotional undercurrents that continue to shape us.”

	It is a story, too, that hits close to home for the director, whose parents divorced when she was a young girl. “The emotion is very personal — the emotion of reconnecting with someone that is supposed to be your father, but you don’t really know him,” she says. 

	That feeling anchors the “unorthodox, unconventional relationship” at the heart of “Hold Onto Me.” “What I cared about a lot was this awkwardness in the beginning, where you’re supposed to love this person — you’re supposed to already have a bond with this person that’s your father, but you don’t,” she says. “So you’re starting to build it, and you don’t even know how to approach it. You’re shy, you’re resisting.” When her own father returned to her life years later, when she was a teenage girl, Aristidou says “he ended up being more of a friend than a father figure.”

	The puckish give-and-take between Iris and Aris that leads to the gradual thaw in their relationship owes to spell-binding performances from Passalis — a Greek Weird Wave stalwart — and Petrova, who was discovered by casting director Daina Papadaki during the search for a non-professional lead.

	“She’s a very mature kid,” Aristidou says. “She’s very deep. She’s very stoic as a person.” When the director told Petrova that she was “going to carry this entire movie” on her young shoulders, Aristidou says the 11-year-old didn’t blink.
	

	The on-screen chemistry between the film’s two stars wasn’t simply a consequence of stellar acting and direction. Passalis, who’d been shooting another film during pre-production for “Hold Onto Me,” was laid low with COVID just as principal photography was about to begin. Cast and crew were left with no time to rehearse.

	“We just read the script the day before the shoot, and then we started shooting,” says Aristidou. “[Petrova] didn’t really like [Passalis] in the beginning. So it was beautiful, because their bond was being built while we were shooting, and it was also happening in the film. That was happening in parallel, while they were getting to know each other in real life,” she adds. “So there’s a lot of truth in their reactions [to each other].”

	Call it serendipity, if you must. But as she begins a historic Oscar campaign for her native Cyprus, Aristidou suggests that perhaps the stars aligned in her favor for a reason, explaining how she’s constantly “open to life and to what it brings.”

	“I’ve learned a lot. And I think the most important was to not push things when they’re not ready to happen. And just to flow,” she says. “I’m a very determined person, so I always had a very clear view of where I wanted to go. And it never worked out that way,” she continues. “I always end up close to where I imagined I would be. But it was through different paths. You can never really plan.”

	The Thessaloniki Film Festival runs Nov. 5 – 15.

schema.headline: ‘Hold Onto Me’ Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: ‘I Really Feel Like We’re Underdogs’

title: Top Limited Series Writers on the Importance of Episode Titles and Adapting Well-Known Films and True Stories: ‘You Come Out With Something Familiar and Surprising’
description: The writers and creators behind some of television’s most popular limited series joined Variety’s A Night in the Writers Room to discuss their crea
body:
The writers and creators behind some of television’s most popular limited series joined Variety’s A Night in the Writers Room to discuss their creative processes behind adapting stories for television.

	Moderated by Variety’s senior artisans editor Jazz Tangcay, the limited series panel featured Nick Antosca of “Cape Fear,” Silka Luisa of “Blade Runner 2099” and Shawn Ryan and Eileen Myers of “American Hostage.”


	Each of the series highlighted during the panel were based on existing stories, whether it was a true-life event or a previously adapted narrative. For Antosca, the challenge was retelling the story of “Cape Fear” after two previous film adaptations. His goal was to make the new version feel fresh while preserving the elements that made the original films resonate with audiences.
	

	“The way I think about adaptations is, I want to create something that’s like the nightmare you have after you saw the original and went to sleep,” he said, earning a laugh from the audience. “You retained some ingredients, the visceral things, and then that mixed together psychologically with other new stuff that you bring to it. So you come out with something that feels, I hope, both familiar and surprising and strange.”

	Luisa faced a similar challenge when reimagining the “Blade Runner” franchise. Set 50 years in the future, the series required Luisa and her team to build on an established world while creating a story that felt distinctly their own.

	“American Hostage,” meanwhile, presented a different set of challenges, as it was based on a true story from 1977. Beyond extensive research consisting of 911 calls, newspapers and court documents, the creative team had to find a way to make the historic events resonate with modern audiences. Ryan shared that while the team felt an obligation to present an honest narrative supported by facts, creative judgement was used to fill in the gaps of what details remained unknown.
	

	Beyond the stories themselves, the panelists also discussed the importance of building the right writers’ room, which they agreed should consist of individuals who bring different strengths to the table. Ryan said his first guideline when assembling a writers room is recognizing his own weaknesses and finding people who can fill those gaps and offer different perspectives.

	“I certainly realize, as a showrunner, that we are missing out on so many perspectives. We are missing out on different life experiences,” he said. “I just learned [to ask], ‘How are these people going to fit in with each other? Where do I need help?’”

	Myers added, “In running a room, I always feel like, around that table, we’re on a boat together. We rise and fall together. And I do feel that best idea wins and also having an openness to people and their experiences.”

	The writers also agreed that chemistry is essential to a successful writers room, which should serve as a space where collaborators can experiment, fail and succeed together.

	“You’re putting it together like a band. It’s like somebody plays guitar, somebody writes for this character,” he explained. “Somebody writes for that character. Somebody brings the humor. Somebody has expertise in spycraft, and you’re thinking about all those things when you’re interviewing writers: How are these guys going to play the song? They can all be great, but if they’re the wrong alchemy, it’s not going to work.”

	That collaboration can extend to details audiences might not immediately notice, including episode titles. The panelists discussed how they approach naming episodes, with some titles serving as Easter eggs or nods to details that didn’t make it to the screen.

	For “American Hostage,” each episode is named after commercials and advertisements featured on WIBC in real life. Meanwhile, the first episode of “Cape Fear,” titled “Fingers & Toes,” references a moment from the 1962 film where Robert Mitchum’s character describes cutting off children’s fingers and toes. 

	But writers can’t bring their visions to life alone. The panelists emphasized the importance of collaborating with department heads, who help translate the scripts into fully realized worlds.

	“When you find those people whom you have a shorthand with, they’re just worth their weight in gold,” Antosca said. “They become your closest collaborators.”
	

	Working closely with department heads was particularly important for “Blade Runner 2099,” given its visual storytelling and narrative that comes from outside the dialogue. Luisa explained that she finds it difficult to write a scene without knowing what the world around the characters looks like.

	“We had HODs [head of departments] from all over the world, craftsmen from all over the world, and each of them interpreted what was written differently,” Luisa said. “And I think we’re living in a time right now where the idea of human craftsmanship is being questioned, and to actually see people collaborate together in a room, and it’s so alive, I just feel so grateful to have had that gift. And I think when I watch the show, that’s the thing: I see everybody’s little voice on screen. It’s the magic.”

schema.headline: Top Limited Series Writers on the Importance of Episode Titles and Adapting Well-Known Films and True Stories: ‘You Come Out With Something Familiar and Surprising’

title: FAA Issues Rare Nationwide Ground Stop, Orders All Flights Halted
body:

                            1:13 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
          UPDATE
  
    
            1:36 PM PT -- Peter Muntean, an Aviation Correspondent for CNN, predicts that this issue may last for days, with one or two days being needed to diagnose the issue. 
      
    
            1:28 PM PT -- U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports follows a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. He says FAA technicians are investigating the issue.
      
    
            Travelers across America are going nowhere fast ... the FAA has ordered an extremely rare nationwide ground stop, bringing departing flights across the country to a screeching halt!
      
    
            The Federal Aviation Administration issued the sweeping order Friday afternoon, citing "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety," according to U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
      
    
      
      Issued by the FAA just moments ago, ALL US airports are currently ground stopped. This means NO flights may depart for US airports. Flights already in the air will be allowed to land. This is related to an FAA equipment outage. https://t.co/wgyuOXeF0k
              @flightradar24
          
  
    
            An air traffic control advisory states ... "All departing traffic should remain ground stopped until further notice."
      

            And even international flights are caught up in the chaos ... the FAA says incoming international flights will be handled on a case-by-case basis.
      
    
            The massive disruption comes as several major airports were already battling delays Friday, including Chicago's O'Hare and Midway airports, which were hit with ground stops tied to equipment outages.
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Meanwhile, San Francisco International Airport reported average ground delays of more than two hours due to wind, while New York's LaGuardia Airport was also dealing with significant delays.
      
    
            It's unclear exactly what prompted the nationwide order or how long planes will be forced to stay on the ground.

title: Earl Thomas’ Wife Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy to Scam $2.7 Million From Ex-NFL Star
description:
Ex-NFL Star Earl Thomas
                          Wife Pleads Guilty To Conspiracy to Scam Him Out Of
body:
Ex-NFL Star Earl Thomas
                          Wife Pleads Guilty To Conspiracy to Scam Him Out Of $2.7 Million
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 13, 2026
                            12:39 PM PST
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Nina Thomas -- the estranged wife of Earl Thomas -- has fallen on her sword in her criminal case, pleading guilty to conspiring to scam her former NFL star husband out of $2.7 million.
      
    
            According to federal court document, obtained by TMZ, Nina will plead guilty to 1 count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud as part of a plea deal with prosecutors, and she faces a maximum of 5 years in prison and/or a $250,000 fine. The judge also ordered Nina and co-defendant Kevin Thompson to be jointly responsible for paying restitution in the amount of $3.497,444.64.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Under the agreement ... Kevin will plead guilty to 2 charges -- conspiracy to commit wire fraud and possession with intent to distribute cocaine. Kevin faces 5 years in prison on the wire fraud charge and/or a fine of $250,000. He also faces up to 40 years in prison on the cocaine distribution charge and a fine of $5 million.
      

            As we previously reported ... in 2024, Nina and Kevin were indicted on federal charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, aggravated identity theft and money laundering. Thompson was also charged with possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of cocaine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Prosecutors said the defendants swindled Earl out of millions of dollars after Nina’s marriage to the ex-Seattle Seahawks free safety went up in smoke.
      
    
            Prosecutors alleged Nina kicked off her scheme to illegally siphon cash from Earl in September 2021 -- after she filed for divorce from him in 2020. The estranged couple got married in 2016 at a lavish ceremony attended by the likes of Russell Wilson and Ciara.
      
    
            Prosecutors accuse Nina and Kevin of taking money from Earl without his knowledge ... and transferring the funds and other property into bank accounts under their control.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The authorities claim the defendants stole more than $2.7 million from the Earl ... and says they made expensive purchases, spending $28,796 on an Hermès Birkin handbag and $52,890 on a Porsche Panamera. Prosecutors also say the two charged $5,500 on Earl’s credit card for a plastic surgery operation.
      
    
            Nina and Kevin were eventually arrested and taken into custody on December 16, 2024.
